# Validation of LLM Ratings

In this document, we check whether LLM ratings align with human ratings collected from 7 raters on 99 chunks across five dimensions (confidence, control, generation, justification, regulation).

Human ratings serve as the gold standard. We can adjust the LLM prompts to better match human judgements, but we shouldn't expect a perfect correlation given the complexity of the task.


```{r chunk-1, include=FALSE}

stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(project_root, "Deliberation.Rproj")))

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
```

```{r chunk-2}
rm(list = ls())
set.seed(123)

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(irr)
library(psych)
library(jtools)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggExtra)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

measures <- c("Generation", "Justification", "Control", "Regulation", "Confidence")

# output directory for saved plots
plot_dir <- "./Output/LLM_scoring_validation"
dir.create(plot_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# pretty-print p-values
format_p <- function(p) {
  if (p < .001) return("< .001")
  return(sprintf("%.3f", p))
}

# significance stars for correlation matrices
star_p <- function(p) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "",
    p < .001 ~ "***",
    p < .01  ~ "**",
    p < .05  ~ "*",
    TRUE     ~ ""
  )
}
```

```{r chunk-3}
# load human ratings (two duplicates are averaged)
validation_ratings_humans <- read_xlsx("./Data/chunk_validation_ratings.xlsx",
                                       sheet = "chunks_2") %>%
  mutate(across(matches("^(Control|Generation|Regulation|Justification|Confidence)"),
                ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.)))) %>%
  group_by(Chunk_text, Question) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(),
                   ~ if (is.numeric(.x)) mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE) else first(.x)),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r chunk-4}
# experiment ids and readable labels
exp_names <- c("unified_v1", "unified_v2", "individual_v1",
               "unified_gpt_v2", "unified_gpt_v3", "unified_gpt_v4", "unified_gpt_v5",
               "unified_gpt_v3_low_reasoning",
               "unified_gpt_v3_medium_reasoning",
               "unified_gpt_v3_high_reasoning")

exp_labels <- c(
  unified_v1                      = "Llama – base prompt",
  unified_v2                      = "Llama – broader Control def.",
  individual_v1                   = "Llama – one call per function",
  unified_gpt_v2                  = "GPT – broader Control def.",
  unified_gpt_v3                  = "GPT – no forced-zero rule",
  unified_gpt_v4                  = "GPT – partial generation counts",
  unified_gpt_v5                  = "GPT – with scoring examples",
  unified_gpt_v3_low_reasoning    = "GPT – low reasoning",
  unified_gpt_v3_medium_reasoning = "GPT – medium reasoning",
  unified_gpt_v3_high_reasoning   = "GPT – high reasoning"
)

# focus experiment for the detailed single-measure plots
exp_focus <- "unified_gpt_v3_low_reasoning"
```

```{r chunk-5}
# helper: average human rater columns for a given measure
compute_human_avg <- function(df, measure) {
  human_cols <- df %>%
    select(starts_with(measure), -matches("_LLM_")) %>%
    names()
  df %>%
    mutate(human_avg = rowMeans(across(all_of(human_cols)), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(human_avg)
}
```

```{r chunk-6}
# load all LLM experiment files and join to human ratings
llm_dir <- "./Output/Prompt_optimization"

read_llm_exp <- function(exp) {
  readr::read_csv(file.path(llm_dir, paste0(exp, ".csv")),
                  show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    rename(Chunk_text = response_text, Question = question_text) %>%
    select(Chunk_text, Question,
           confidence_mean, control_mean,
           generation_mean, justification_mean, regulation_mean) %>%
    rename(Confidence = confidence_mean,
           Control = control_mean,
           Generation = generation_mean,
           Justification = justification_mean,
           Regulation = regulation_mean) %>%
    rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_LLM_", exp), .cols = any_of(measures))
}

# join all experiments to human data in one pass
validation_ratings_joined <- exp_names %>%
  map(read_llm_exp) %>%
  reduce(left_join, by = c("Chunk_text", "Question")) %>%
  left_join(validation_ratings_humans, ., by = c("Chunk_text", "Question"))
```

```{r chunk-7}
# build the master long dataframe used throughout: human_avg vs llm per measure × experiment
get_cor_df <- function(measure) {
  human_avg <- compute_human_avg(validation_ratings_joined, measure)
  validation_ratings_joined %>%
    mutate(human_avg = human_avg) %>%
    select(human_avg, matches(paste0("^", measure, "_LLM_"))) %>%
    pivot_longer(-human_avg, names_to = "col", values_to = "llm_raw") %>%
    mutate(Experiment = str_remove(col, paste0("^", measure, "_LLM_")),
           Measure = measure) %>%
    filter(Experiment %in% exp_names) %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    mutate(Experiment = recode(Experiment, !!!exp_labels),
           Experiment = factor(Experiment,
                               levels = unname(exp_labels[exp_names]))) %>%
    select(Measure, Experiment, human_avg, llm_raw)
}

cor_long_all <- map_dfr(measures, get_cor_df)
```

## Inter-Rater Reliability (ICC) among Human Raters

Before comparing LLM ratings to human ratings, we first check how consistent the human raters are with each other. We use the consistency form of the ICC because we care about relative ranking, not absolute values.

```{r chunk-8}
# compute ICC for each measure
icc_results <- map_dfr(measures, function(m) {
  mat <- validation_ratings_joined %>%
    select(starts_with(m), -matches("_LLM_")) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
    drop_na()
  
  icc_out <- irr::icc(mat, model = "twoway", type = "consistency", unit = "average")
  tibble(
    Measure = m,
    ICC     = round(icc_out$value, 2),
    Lower95 = round(icc_out$lbound, 2),
    Upper95 = round(icc_out$ubound, 2),
    p_value = format_p(icc_out$p.value)
  )
})

icc_results %>%
  kable(caption = "Inter-rater reliability (ICC, two-way consistency, average measures)",
        align = "c") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center")
```

Confidence is excellent (> .90), while Control is the lowest at 0.74 but still acceptable.

## Correlation between LLMs and Human Raters

We compare each LLM experiment to the averaged human ratings using Spearman correlations. We use Spearman  here because some distributions are not normal.

### Scatter plots with marginal distributions


```{r chunk-9, fig.width=6, fig.height=6}
# scatter + marginal histograms for every experiment × measure
for (exp in levels(cor_long_all$Experiment)) {
  exp_df <- cor_long_all %>% filter(Experiment == exp)

  for (m in measures) {
    plot_df <- filter(exp_df, Measure == m)
    rho <- cor(plot_df$human_avg, plot_df$llm_raw, method = "spearman")

    p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = human_avg, y = llm_raw)) +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
                  linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 2) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#E63946", linewidth = 0.8) +
      annotate("text", x = 8, y = 95,
               label = sprintf("rho == %.2f", rho), parse = TRUE,
               size = 4.5, hjust = 0) +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100)) +
      labs(x = "Average human rating", y = "LLM rating",
           title = paste0(m, " — ", exp)) +
      theme_apa()

    print(ggMarginal(p, type = "histogram", fill = "gray80", color = "white", bins = 20))
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}
```

### Detailed correlations for the focus experiment (`unified_gpt_v3_low_reasoning`)

We zoom in on our focus experiment and plot, for each of the five measures, the scatter of LLM ratings against averaged human ratings, with a GAM smooth and the Spearman correlation reported in APA style. Axes share the same 0–100 scale and a 1:1 reference line is shown for context.

```{r chunk-10, fig.width=16, fig.height=4.2}

focus_label <- exp_labels[[exp_focus]]

# colors for each deliberation function
function_colors <- c(
  "Generation"    = "royalblue3",
  "Justification" = "gold3",
  "Control"       = "firebrick3",
  "Regulation"    = "forestgreen",
  "Confidence"    = "deepskyblue"
)

# APA-style formatter for the (rho, p) annotation
apa_corr_label <- function(rho, p) {
  rho_str <- sprintf("%.2f", abs(rho))
  rho_str <- sub("^0", "", rho_str)

  if (rho < 0) {
    rho_str <- paste0("-", rho_str)
  }

  if (p < .001) {
    p_str <- "italic(p) < .001"
  } else {
    p_formatted <- sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p))
    p_str <- sprintf("italic(p) == '%s'", p_formatted)
  }

  sprintf("italic(rho) == '%s' * ',' ~ %s", rho_str, p_str)
}

# compute correlations once for both the plots and the table
correlation_results <- map_dfr(names(function_colors), function(m) {
  d <- cor_long_all %>%
    filter(Experiment == focus_label,
           Measure == m) %>%
    drop_na(human_avg, llm_raw)

  ct <- psych::corr.test(d$human_avg,
                         d$llm_raw,
                         method = "spearman",
                         adjust = "none")

  tibble(Measure = m,
         rho = unname(ct$r)[1],
         Lower95 = unname(ct$ci$lower)[1],
         Upper95 = unname(ct$ci$upper)[1],
         p = unname(ct$p)[1])
})

make_scatter_plot <- function(m, xlab = NULL, ylab = NULL) {
  d <- cor_long_all %>%
    filter(Experiment == focus_label,
           Measure == m) %>%
    drop_na(human_avg, llm_raw)

  result <- correlation_results %>%
    filter(Measure == m)

  label_expr <- apa_corr_label(result$rho, result$p)

  ggplot(d, aes(x = human_avg, y = llm_raw)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1,
                intercept = 0,
                linetype = "dashed",
                colour = "grey60",
                linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6,
               size = 2,
               colour = function_colors[[m]]) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm",
                se = TRUE,
                colour = "black",
                fill = "grey70",
                alpha = 0.25,
                linewidth = 0.7) +
    annotate("text",
             x = 3,
             y = 96,
             hjust = 0,
             label = label_expr,
             parse = TRUE,
             size = 4.5) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 1,
                xlim = c(0, 100),
                ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
    labs(x = xlab,
         y = ylab,
         title = m) +
    theme_apa() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5,
                                    size = 13,
                                    face = "bold"),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
          plot.margin = margin(6, 8, 4, 8))
}

# y label on leftmost (Generation), x label on middle (Control), none elsewhere
scatter_plots <- list(
  make_scatter_plot("Generation", ylab = "LLM rating"),
  make_scatter_plot("Justification"),
  make_scatter_plot("Control", xlab = "Average human rating"),
  make_scatter_plot("Regulation"),
  make_scatter_plot("Confidence")
)

scatterplot_LLM_humans_gpt5_1_low <- ggarrange(
  plotlist = scatter_plots,
  ncol = 3,
  nrow = 2,
  align = "hv"
)

scatterplot_LLM_humans_gpt5_1_low

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "scatterplot_LLM_humans_gpt5_1_low.svg"),
       scatterplot_LLM_humans_gpt5_1_low,
       width = 10,
       height = 8)

correlation_results %>%
  mutate(`Spearman's ρ [95% CI]` = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]",
                                           rho,
                                           Lower95,
                                           Upper95),
         p = map_chr(p, format_p)) %>%
  select(Measure,
         `Spearman's ρ [95% CI]`,
         p) %>%
  kable(caption = "Spearman correlations between average human ratings and LLM ratings.")

```

### Spearman coefficients across experiments

The horizontal plot below shows Spearman ρ with bootstrapped 95% CIs for every measure × experiment, sorted by average performance. Experiments are ordered by mean ρ across measures.

```{r chunk-12, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# spearman correlation with bootstrapped CI
cor_with_ci <- function(x, y, conf_level = 0.95, n_boot = 2000, seed = 123) {
  df <- tibble(x = x, y = y) %>% drop_na()
  r <- cor(df$x, df$y, method = "spearman")
  set.seed(seed)
  boot_r <- replicate(n_boot, {
    idx <- sample.int(nrow(df), replace = TRUE)
    cor(df$x[idx], df$y[idx], method = "spearman")
  })
  alpha <- (1 - conf_level) / 2
  tibble(r = unname(r),
         conf_low = quantile(boot_r, alpha, na.rm = TRUE),
         conf_high = quantile(boot_r, 1 - alpha, na.rm = TRUE),
         n = nrow(df))
}

# build summary across all measures × experiments
cor_sum_spearman <- cor_long_all %>%
  group_by(Measure, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(tmp = list(cor_with_ci(human_avg, llm_raw)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest(tmp)

# order experiments by their average rho
exp_order <- cor_sum_spearman %>%
  group_by(Experiment) %>%
  summarise(mean_r = mean(r, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_r)) %>%
  pull(Experiment)

cor_sum_spearman <- cor_sum_spearman %>%
  mutate(Experiment = factor(Experiment, levels = exp_order),
         Measure = factor(Measure, levels = measures))

x_pad <- 0.03
x_lim <- c(min(cor_sum_spearman$conf_low, na.rm = TRUE) - x_pad - 0.05,
            max(cor_sum_spearman$conf_high, na.rm = TRUE) + x_pad + 0.05)

p_spearman <- ggplot(cor_sum_spearman, aes(x = r, y = Experiment, color = Experiment)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), height = 0.15) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)),
            vjust = -0.8, size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ Measure, scales = "fixed") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = x_lim) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
  labs(x = "Spearman ρ", y = NULL) +
  theme_apa() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_spearman

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "spearman_coefficients_across_experiments.svg"),
       p_spearman, width = 10, height = 8)
```

## Intercorrelation Structure: Humans vs LLMs

Finally, we compare the intercorrelation pattern across constructs for humans and each LLM experiment. If the LLM captures the same latent structure as human raters, the matrices should look similar. We drop Confidence since it is conceptually distinct from the four deliberation functions.

```{r chunk-13, fig.width=14, fig.height=12}
measures_mat <- setdiff(measures, "Confidence")

# lower-triangle pearson correlation matrix in long format
cor_mat_long <- function(df_wide, vars, panel_label) {
  dat <- df_wide %>% select(all_of(vars)) %>% drop_na()
  idx_tbl <- tibble(var = vars, idx = seq_along(vars))

  crossing(var1 = vars, var2 = vars) %>%
    mutate(
      r = map2_dbl(var1, var2, ~ cor(dat[[.x]], dat[[.y]])),
      p = map2_dbl(var1, var2,
                   ~ suppressWarnings(cor.test(dat[[.x]], dat[[.y]])$p.value)),
      stars = star_p(p),
      panel = panel_label
    ) %>%
    left_join(idx_tbl, by = c("var1" = "var")) %>% rename(i = idx) %>%
    left_join(idx_tbl, by = c("var2" = "var")) %>% rename(j = idx) %>%
    mutate(across(c(r, p), ~ if_else(j > i, NA_real_, .x)),
           stars = if_else(j > i, NA_character_, stars)) %>%
    select(panel, var1, var2, r, p, stars) %>%
    mutate(var1 = factor(var1, levels = vars),
           var2 = factor(var2, levels = vars),
           label = if_else(is.na(r), "",
                           paste0(sprintf("%.2f", r), stars)))
}

# human averages in wide format
human_wide <- map_dfr(measures_mat, function(m) {
  validation_ratings_joined %>%
    transmute(Chunk_text, Question, Measure = m,
              value = compute_human_avg(validation_ratings_joined, m))
}) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Measure, values_from = value)

# human panel
human_cor <- cor_mat_long(human_wide, measures_mat, "Humans")

# one panel per LLM experiment
llm_cor <- map_dfr(exp_names, function(exp) {
  llm_cols <- paste0(measures_mat, "_LLM_", exp)
  llm_wide <- validation_ratings_joined %>%
    select(Chunk_text, Question, any_of(llm_cols)) %>%
    rename_with(~ str_replace(.x, paste0("_LLM_", exp, "$"), ""),
                any_of(llm_cols))
  cor_mat_long(llm_wide, measures_mat, exp_labels[[exp]])
})

# combine with humans first, then experiments in order
panel_levels <- c("Humans", unname(exp_labels[exp_names]))
plot_long <- bind_rows(human_cor, llm_cor) %>%
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = panel_levels))

p_intercor <- ggplot(plot_long, aes(x = var2, y = var1, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 4, axes = "all") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(limits = c(-1, 1),
                       low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       na.value = "white") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "r") +
  theme_apa() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 7))

p_intercor

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "intercorrelation_humans_vs_llms.svg"),
       p_intercor, width = 14, height = 12)
```
